questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city had to be a good size for studying. The weather had to be good. The university should not be bad. The destination should not be too far from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Administration was a bit tough from University of Bologna and it took at lot of time so therefore I do not give 10. But now after the exchange I do not see it as a big of a problem as when I had to fight with it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was possible via the university's website, which was quite good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Great assistance via email every time I had a question.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You just need to remember that it is an Italian university so everything moves slower than in Denmark but eventually it works.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. Housing is very limited in Bologna especially for long term stays. If you do not wish to spend ages searching on Facebook sites with a lot of scammers then I recommend you contact some of the big private housing lenders. Check out "The Social Hub" and "Laude living". A good agency if you are a couple of students who wants to live together is "Urnest" who rent of entire apartments. But here you need to do it very early and pay the price (at least 1000 euro per month), but I would say that is totally worth it due the opportunity cost of searching and possible scamming that you will not have. However, I was not fast enough.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You need to start looking very early! It is quite expensive in Bologna. Do not expect to get a room for less than 600 euros per month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This will be you biggest issue at the mobility.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy through a portal online much like at KU, but less binding and more flexible. You can change courses even after the first lectures.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guides

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything. No problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very easy and flexible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was much like at KU. Some of them more easy than others (like at KU).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depends from course to course. But in general it is more engaging than at KU. Students actually ask questions and the teacher wants you to do that. One of the courses was very much like a proper seminar with discussions and texts for each lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public Economics, Advanced Topics in Liquidity Management in the Post Crisis Era, History of Economic Thought, Computer Programming, Advanced Interest Rate Models and Markets.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of the listed courses!
Public economics: You go from basic knowledge from Micro II and Macro III and then read top academic papers. Very nice professor! 

Adv. Liquidity management: Finally a course on actual monetary policy! This is lacking so much at polit. You learn how ECB conducts MP! And how the baking sector absorbs and amplifies shocks in connection to the central bank and real economy. Best course in my life. Professor is so nice. The curriculum even included this year's nobel price winners paper (before the winner was announced). 

History: Very good professor and quite demanding course. Lots of readings due to discussion of papers each lecture. But very nice and a feeling of a proper seminar. Very academic. Not just 3 hour closed book exam. 

Programming: You should not know python before this course! It starts from the very basics. So you would be bored if you knew it already. It was good for beginners and still demanding. It was good that I already knew som Matlab from the SVAR course a KU. 

Adv. interest models. Extremely difficult course. Continuous time finance with a physicists as professor. This is like the courses at mat.øk . If you want to understand everything you need to have "mål og integralteori" from mat.øk and some previous introducing continuous finance courses. It is not enough to have attended e.g Fin 1 and from mat.øk and financial theory and models from polit. However, I had only attended those courses and I still completed with highest score as I was in a very good group for the exam and I spend a lot of time. In the end the exam is about pricing instruments so you need to apply the theory which saved me although there still was a proof in the exam which the group could do together. The professor is probably the most competent man on the planet for this course so a very good course if you want to be "quant" after your studies (or just understand what they are doing).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had dinner maybe four times a week at restaurants which are extremely cheap compared to Denmark. Groceries are the same price as in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unibo did not hos anything, but is was so easy to done nice things in Bologna.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel with train is so easy. Bologna is really well placed for this!!! Go wherever you want. You can also fly easily to southern Italy as the airport is 7 (yes seven) minutes away from the city center in train. Eat a lot of food! It is soooo good. Bologna is the food center of Italy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Eat, eat and eat. Bologna is called the "fat city" for a purpose!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took a few days to get used to the crazy traffic. But then it is easy. They are very open minded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Drink apperitivos and go to parties. They love to just drink outside and squares.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The trafic is f****d! Be very carefull if you rent a car and when just walking around. The city is not made for biking so take care when you bike.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italians are lovely and the food is fantastic

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in advance (10 months before), travel, eat.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm when the administration does not answer you fast. They will eventually and everything will work out fine for your exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The university was very good. Better than expected. I learned a lot and still had time to travel and enjoy the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: They have quarters and not semester so you need to get used to having more exams and a lot of reading for each course in a short time period.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Bologna. It is a fantastic city to live in a a student. Much better than Copenhagen due to the size. Alcohol and food is cheap. (1L aperol for 10 euros at a student bar).

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
